key_gap: The AI reached the same final verdict as the human (no incremental lift; reject replication; propose an RCT) but discovered the counter-data opportunistically: it ran the lateral control check early and the compositional check mid-process, yet the temporal class — both regions jumping ~+35% in the launch quarter (a shared market event) — surfaced only in the REVIEW stage, after one extra pass. The human's single lens ('what does this story leave out?') demanded all three counter-data classes (lateral, temporal, compositional) before writing a conclusion and centered the verdict on the differential (0.7 ± 4 pp), not the +45% headline.
learning_signal: Narrative Fallacy Detection is a systematic selection audit: against any causal narrative, sweep three orthogonal classes of counter-data — lateral (a comparison group without the intervention), temporal (pre-intervention slope plus the boundary jump at the intervention point), and compositional (which sub-population or account rows carry the delta). Each class is independently decisive; missing one leaves a plausible alternative explanation standing (here: a shared market event). The verdict is the differential against all three, stated with its noise, never the story's headline.
suggested_improvement: Add a WHY-stage 'counter-data sweep' gate: before accepting any causal narrative (and before drafting the conclusion), the agent must record, for each of the three classes, either the relevant comparison numbers or an explicit 'not applicable / unavailable' note: (1) lateral — control group without the intervention; (2) temporal — pre-period trend and boundary difference at the intervention point; (3) compositional — contribution/concentration of the delta. Fail the gate if fewer than two classes are covered; require the decision packet to state the story's strongest contradiction, not its strongest support, and to quote the differential with its noise.

key_gap: The pure human-style trace executed the model's registered failure mode ('can dismiss real patterns'): it treated a genuine randomized controlled pilot (n = 1,000/arm; diff 3.9 pt; CI [2.8, 5.0]; p < 0.001; 12-week cohort stability 3.5–4.2) and a pre-specified activation mechanism chain as 'a story told by the team that needs it true,' demanded a longer, all-platform, independently analyzed trial, and declined the decision indefinitely — incurring the stated delay cost (~2,000 churned users/month). The AI scoped its doubt: internal-validity doubt (selection, confounding) is answered by the randomization itself — the control arm is exactly the counter-data the skeptic's lens demands — while external-validity doubt (mobile-only pilot, novelty, long-run drift) was converted into a 10% holdout + monitoring + revert trigger, and it committed to rollout.
learning_signal: Narrative skepticism needs a stopping rule and a scope classifier. Classify each doubt as internal-validity (selection, confounding, cherry-picking — answered by design: randomization, control arm, pre-specified metrics) or external-validity/generalization (answered only by rollout monitoring). A doubt already answered by the design must be dropped, not repeated. When a pattern is supported by a controlled experiment plus an independently specified mechanism, the narrative IS the evidence; skepticism's job switches from doubting the pattern to bounding its generalization, and the decision terminates in an action with a monitoring plan — never in indefinite postponement, because delay has a cost.
suggested_improvement: Add a REVIEW-stage 'skepticism-scope' check: (1) list every doubt raised; (2) classify each as internal-validity or external-validity; (3) for internal doubts, verify against the study design — if the design controls them (randomization, control arm, pre-specified metrics), remove them from the packet; (4) for external doubts, attach a monitoring/guardrail action (holdout, revert trigger, review date); (5) require the packet to terminate in SOLVED or APPROXIMATED with a committed decision and monitoring plan, and forbid NEEDS_EVIDENCE when the available evidence is already decision-grade.
